settings.description: §11.1 — the alpha-mode tier-0 layout, which ships today with no evidence behind it. The opaque row was rebalanced to L 28 @ 4 / C 15 @ 3; alpha mode still carries v0.6's L 20 @ 5 / C 9 @ 4 only because the photographic corpus has no transparency. Every arm is exactly 32 bytes (249-256 bits: 54 prefix + 9 alpha DC/scale + L*lb + 2*C*cb + 5*4 alpha AC). Alpha AC is held at the shipped 5 @ 4 so the question stays how luma and chroma should split the alpha-mode budget; SS11.3 sweeps the alpha fields themselves. Scored over three backdrops with a direct alpha-plane MAE, because a single white backdrop hides most alpha error. Every arm pins `alpha_ac_count` and `alpha_ac_bits` explicitly. A config that overrides only part of a layout inherits the rest from Tunables::DEFAULT, so when the default alpha allocation changed in §11.3 these arms silently stopped being 32 bytes — the same class of drift the corpus pins exist to prevent, in the knob space rather than the corpus.
